name: ChatGPT
summary: A general-purpose AI chat assistant for writing, explaining, planning and simple code and image tasks.
strengths: a familiar chat interface
one place for text, images and code help
watchOutFor: It can state wrong facts with confidence. Check anything important.
Free limits and features change often.

name: Claude
summary: An AI chat assistant for writing, analysing long documents, explaining ideas and helping with code.
strengths: readable long-form writing
working with long pasted documents
watchOutFor: It can state wrong facts with confidence. Check anything important.
Free usage limits can run out mid-task.

name: Gemini
summary: Google's AI assistant, connected to Google accounts and apps such as Gmail, Docs and Drive.
strengths: tight links with your Google account and apps
an assistant you may already have access to
watchOutFor: It can state wrong facts with confidence. Check anything important.
Features differ between personal and work accounts.

name: Microsoft Copilot
summary: Microsoft's AI assistant, available in the browser, in Windows and inside Microsoft 365 apps.
strengths: sign-in with a Microsoft account
help inside Word, PowerPoint and Windows
watchOutFor: Some features need a paid Microsoft 365 plan.
It can state wrong facts with confidence.

name: Perplexity
summary: An AI answer engine that searches the web and shows the pages it used for each answer.
strengths: answers that link to the pages they used
quick background reading on a topic
watchOutFor: A link does not prove the summary is right. Open the source.
Web pages it cites can be wrong or biased.

name: NotebookLM
summary: A Google tool that answers questions using only the documents and links you add to a notebook.
strengths: answers grounded in your own files
summaries and study aids made from your material
watchOutFor: It is only as good as the files you give it.
Check its quotes against the original pages.

name: Elicit
summary: An AI research assistant that finds academic papers and pulls key details out of them.
strengths: finding and comparing academic papers
a table of what each paper says
watchOutFor: It focuses on academic papers, so it is weaker for general web questions.
Read the paper before you rely on an extracted detail.

name: Google Scholar
summary: A search engine for scholarly papers, books and citations.
strengths: a free search across scholarly papers
a quick way to see who cited a paper
watchOutFor: Not every paper it finds is free to read.
It lists papers but does not judge their quality.

name: Project Gutenberg
summary: A library of free ebooks whose copyright has expired, including many classic and translated works.
strengths: free ebooks you can read or download
well-known translations of older works
watchOutFor: Translations can be old and dated in language.
Note which edition and translator you read.

name: Internet Archive
summary: A digital library of scanned books, old publications, recordings and archived web pages.
strengths: scanned books and older publications
texts that are hard to find elsewhere
watchOutFor: Scans can be hard to search or read.
Borrowing rules apply to some books.

name: Sacred Texts Archive
summary: A website with translations of religious, mythological and folklore texts from many traditions, including Indian ones.
strengths: translations of epics, scriptures and folklore
texts from many cultures in one place
watchOutFor: Most translations are older public-domain ones. Name the translator when you quote.
It is not a scholarly edition. Cross-check key claims.

name: GitHub Copilot
summary: An AI coding helper that suggests code and answers questions inside your code editor.
strengths: suggestions as you type in your editor
support for many editors and languages
watchOutFor: Review every suggestion. It can write insecure or wrong code.
Students and teachers may have separate access terms.

name: Cursor
summary: A code editor built around AI, which can answer questions about your project and edit several files at once.
strengths: an editor designed around AI help
edits that span several files
watchOutFor: It is easy to accept changes you have not read.
Usage limits on free plans can end a session early.

name: Claude Code
summary: A command-line AI coding assistant that reads your project and makes changes you approve.
strengths: working through a whole project from the terminal
step-by-step changes you can review
watchOutFor: You need to be comfortable with the command line and Git.
Review every change before you keep it.

name: Replit
summary: An online workspace where you can write, run and share code in the browser with AI help.
strengths: coding and running a project with nothing to install
sharing a working project by link
watchOutFor: Free plan limits on AI help and hosting can change.
Projects can be tied to the platform.

name: Lovable
summary: An AI app builder that turns a plain-language description into a working web app draft.
strengths: a working app draft from a description
no setup on your computer
watchOutFor: The draft can hide bugs. Test every feature before sharing.
Check login and data rules carefully before real users arrive.

name: v0
summary: An AI tool from Vercel that generates web interface code from a text description.
strengths: interface code from a text description
output that fits React projects
watchOutFor: Read the generated code before you ship it.
It is aimed at React, so it suits React projects best.

name: Midjourney
summary: An AI image generator known for artistic, stylised pictures made from text prompts.
strengths: striking, artistic images
a large community sharing prompts
watchOutFor: Check the terms before using images commercially.
Text inside images is often wrong.

name: Stable Diffusion
summary: A family of open image-generation models you can run on your own computer or through other apps.
strengths: running on your own computer
many community-made models and add-ons
watchOutFor: You need a capable computer and some setup.
Each model has its own licence. Read it before commercial use.

name: Adobe Firefly
summary: Adobe's AI image generator, also built into Adobe apps such as Photoshop and Express.
strengths: a simple web interface
close links with Adobe apps
watchOutFor: Generation credits are limited on free use.
Check the licence terms for your kind of use.

name: Runway
summary: An AI video tool that creates and edits short clips from text, images or existing video.
strengths: generating short clips from a description
AI tools for changing existing footage
watchOutFor: Clip length and credits are limited. Check before planning a long video.
Results vary a lot between tries.

name: Luma Dream Machine
summary: An AI video generator from Luma AI that makes short clips from text prompts or still images.
strengths: turning a still image into a moving clip
a simple prompt-based interface
watchOutFor: Clips are short and credits are limited.
Faces and hands can look wrong.

name: HeyGen
summary: An AI video tool that makes presenter-style videos from a script, with a digital avatar and voice.
strengths: a presenter video from a written script
many languages and voices
watchOutFor: Use only faces and voices you have permission to use.
Viewers may find avatar videos less personal.

name: CapCut
summary: A video editor for phones and computers with templates, captions and effects.
strengths: quick edits with templates and automatic captions
short vertical videos
watchOutFor: Check that it is available where you live. Some countries restrict it.
Some effects and exports may need a paid plan.

name: Clipchamp
summary: A simple video editor from Microsoft that runs in the browser and on Windows.
strengths: a plain timeline that is easy to learn
nothing to install when used in the browser
watchOutFor: It has fewer advanced features than professional editors.
Export quality options may depend on your plan.

name: DaVinci Resolve
summary: A professional video editing and colour-grading program with a free version.
strengths: professional editing and colour tools
a free version for desktop computers
watchOutFor: It needs a fairly powerful computer.
The learning curve is steep for a first video.

name: Adobe Premiere Pro
summary: A professional timeline-based video editor from Adobe.
strengths: a professional editor used widely in the industry
close links with other Adobe apps
watchOutFor: It is a subscription product, with a trial rather than a free plan.
Powerful but takes time to learn.

name: Descript
summary: An editor that turns speech into text so you can edit audio and video by editing the transcript.
strengths: editing talk-based video by editing the transcript
removing filler words quickly
watchOutFor: Check the transcript for errors before you rely on it.
Free plans limit transcription and exports.

name: ElevenLabs
summary: An AI voice tool that turns text into natural-sounding speech in many voices and languages.
strengths: natural-sounding voiceovers
many languages and accents
watchOutFor: Clone only voices you have permission to use.
Check the licence if you publish the audio commercially.

name: Audacity
summary: A free, open-source program for recording and editing audio.
strengths: free recording and clean-up of audio
full control over each track
watchOutFor: It is not an AI voice tool. It records and edits sound only.
The interface takes time to learn.

name: Gamma
summary: An AI presentation tool that builds a slide deck, document or page from a short prompt.
strengths: a full draft deck from a short prompt
quick restyling of the whole deck
watchOutFor: Generated slides still need your facts checked and your own words.
Exporting may be limited on free plans.

name: Google Slides
summary: A browser-based slide editor in Google's office suite, with real-time sharing.
strengths: free sharing and joint editing with a Google account
nothing to install
watchOutFor: It has fewer design extras than dedicated tools.
Complex animation is limited.

name: Microsoft PowerPoint
summary: Microsoft's slide presentation program, available on desktop, mobile and the web.
strengths: familiar to schools and offices
works offline on a computer
watchOutFor: Some features need a paid Microsoft 365 plan.
Files may look different on another computer if fonts are missing.

name: Canva
summary: An easy browser-based design app with templates for slides, posters, resumes, social posts and simple videos.
strengths: thousands of ready templates
design work without design training
watchOutFor: Some templates, images and tools are paid-only.
Popular templates are easy to recognise. Change them.

name: Grammarly
summary: A writing assistant that checks grammar, spelling, clarity and tone as you type.
strengths: fixing grammar and tone as you type
a browser extension for email and documents
watchOutFor: It suggests. You decide. Do not accept every change.
Your text is sent to its servers. Read its privacy terms.

name: LanguageTool
summary: A grammar and style checker with an open-source core that supports many languages.
strengths: checking text in many languages
an open-source core you can run yourself
watchOutFor: Its free version has limits.
It catches errors but does not improve your argument.

name: Notion
summary: A workspace for notes, tables, task lists and planning pages, with optional AI features.
strengths: notes, tables and plans in one place
templates for study and planning
watchOutFor: It can get complicated. Start with one page.
AI features may need a paid plan.

name: Obsidian
summary: A note-taking app that stores notes as plain files on your device and links them together.
strengths: notes kept as plain files on your own device
links between notes that build a map of ideas
watchOutFor: Syncing across devices may cost extra.
It takes time to set up a system that suits you.

name: Anki
summary: A flashcard program that schedules reviews using spaced repetition.
strengths: spaced repetition that schedules reviews for you
a very large library of shared decks
watchOutFor: The interface takes a little time to learn.
The iPhone app may be paid.

name: Quizlet
summary: A study app for making flashcards and practising with quizzes and games.
strengths: quick flashcard sets and practice modes
shared sets from other students
watchOutFor: Some study modes may need a paid plan.
Shared sets can contain mistakes.

name: Astro themes
summary: A catalogue of ready-made website themes for the Astro framework, free and paid.
strengths: finished layouts for portfolios, blogs and business sites
fast pages with little code
watchOutFor: Most themes need a build step and some command-line use.
Check each theme's licence.

name: Framer
summary: A visual website builder and design tool with templates, publishing built in.
strengths: designing and publishing a site visually
built-in animation effects
watchOutFor: Your site lives on its platform. Check what you can export.
Custom domains may need a paid plan.

name: Webflow
summary: A visual website builder that gives detailed control over layout without writing code.
strengths: detailed layout control without code
built-in hosting and content editing
watchOutFor: It has a learning curve.
Hosting and site plans have limits you should check.

name: Wix
summary: A drag-and-drop website builder with many templates and built-in hosting.
strengths: a drag-and-drop editor with many templates
hosting, forms and shop tools in one place
watchOutFor: Moving your site to another service later can be difficult.
Your own domain may need a paid plan.

name: shadcn/ui
summary: A set of accessible React interface components that you copy into your project and change freely.
strengths: components you own and can change freely
accessible building blocks
watchOutFor: It expects React and Tailwind CSS.
Left unchanged, every site built with it looks alike.

name: MUI
summary: A large library of ready-made React components, previously known as Material UI.
strengths: a large, mature set of components
lots of documentation and examples
watchOutFor: The default look is easy to recognise. Customise it.
Some advanced components may be paid.

name: daisyUI
summary: A plugin for Tailwind CSS that adds ready-made component styles and themes, including dark mode.
strengths: component styles through simple class names
built-in colour themes, including dark mode
watchOutFor: It needs Tailwind CSS set up first.
Themes can make sites look alike.

name: Motion
summary: An animation library for React and JavaScript, formerly known as Framer Motion.
strengths: smooth animation with little code
entrance, layout and gesture effects
watchOutFor: Heavy motion slows pages. Respect reduced-motion settings.
You need to know basic React.

name: GSAP
summary: A JavaScript animation library for detailed, timed and scroll-driven animation on web pages.
strengths: fine control over complex sequences
scroll-triggered animation
watchOutFor: The learning curve is steep.
Check the licence terms for your kind of use.

name: Lottie
summary: A format and player for small vector animations exported from design tools and used on web pages and apps.
strengths: playing animations made by a designer
small files compared with video
watchOutFor: Large animations slow down a page.
You still need a tool to make the animation.

name: Next.js
summary: A React framework for building websites and web apps with pages, routing and server features.
strengths: routing, rendering and a large ecosystem
pairing with many hosting options
watchOutFor: You need to know React first.
Its server features take time to learn.

name: React
summary: A JavaScript library for building interactive user interfaces from reusable components.
strengths: a huge community and many tutorials
components you can reuse
watchOutFor: It is a library, not a full framework. You choose routing and structure yourself.
Beginners face many setup choices.

name: Astro
summary: A web framework for fast, content-focused sites that can still use React and other tools.
strengths: fast, mostly static sites for content
using React or other tools only where needed
watchOutFor: It is less suited to apps with many interactive screens.
You still need some HTML and command-line comfort.

name: Expo
summary: A toolset built on React Native for making Android and iOS apps with JavaScript.
strengths: building phone apps with React skills
testing on your own phone quickly
watchOutFor: Publishing to app stores has its own steps and fees.
It suits mobile apps, not ordinary websites.

name: Sanity
summary: A hosted content system with an editing studio that you shape to fit your content.
strengths: flexible, developer-friendly content editing
a hosted service with nothing to run yourself
watchOutFor: A developer needs to set up the editing studio.
Free limits and plans may change.

name: Strapi
summary: An open-source content system you run yourself, with a ready admin panel and an API.
strengths: an admin panel without writing one
open source, so you control your data
watchOutFor: Self-hosting means you run and secure the server.
A hosted version, if you want one, is a paid service.

name: WordPress
summary: A widely used open-source system for running a blog or website, with themes and plugins.
strengths: a huge range of themes and plugins
editing posts and pages without code
watchOutFor: Keep plugins and themes updated. Old ones are a security risk.
Hosting is a separate cost.

name: Supabase
summary: An open-source back end that offers a Postgres database, sign-in and file storage.
strengths: a full database with sign-in built in
an open-source base you can move away from
watchOutFor: Learn its access rules before storing private data.
Free projects may pause when unused.

name: Firebase
summary: Google's app platform with a database, sign-in, file storage and hosting.
strengths: quick set-up for web and mobile apps
database, sign-in and hosting in one place
watchOutFor: Costs can grow with usage. Set budget alerts.
Data is shaped for its own model, which can make later moves harder.

name: MongoDB Atlas
summary: A hosted document database from MongoDB, where data is stored as flexible JSON-like records.
strengths: flexible records without fixed tables
a hosted service that scales
watchOutFor: Check free tier limits before relying on it.
Flexible data still needs a plan to stay tidy.

name: Auth.js
summary: An open-source library that adds sign-in with Google, GitHub, email and other providers to a web app.
strengths: open-source sign-in with no per-user fee
sign-in through many providers
watchOutFor: You manage more of the set-up yourself.
Security details matter. Follow the documentation closely.

name: Clerk
summary: A hosted sign-in service with ready-made sign-up and account screens for web apps.
strengths: ready-made sign-in and account screens
quick set-up
watchOutFor: Free limits and per-user costs can change.
Your users' accounts live on its service.

name: Auth0
summary: A hosted identity service for sign-in, with support for many login methods and company accounts.
strengths: a mature service with many sign-in options
support for company and enterprise logins
watchOutFor: It can be complex to configure.
Costs can rise with the number of users.

name: Razorpay
summary: An Indian payment gateway for UPI, cards and netbanking, with no-code payment links and developer tools.
strengths: UPI, cards and netbanking for Indian customers
payment links that need no code
watchOutFor: You need to complete business verification before taking real payments.
Check fees and settlement times.

name: Cashfree Payments
summary: An Indian payment gateway and payouts service for businesses and developers.
strengths: Indian payment methods and payouts
developer documentation
watchOutFor: Check fees and settlement times.
Real payments need business verification.

name: PayU
summary: An Indian payment gateway that accepts cards, netbanking, UPI and wallets.
strengths: an established gateway for Indian merchants
many payment methods
watchOutFor: Check fees and onboarding steps.
Real payments need business verification.

name: Vercel
summary: A hosting service that publishes a site from a Git repository and gives each change a preview link.
strengths: a live site on every push to Git
preview links for each change
watchOutFor: Free plans can limit commercial use.
Check bandwidth and function limits.

name: Netlify
summary: A hosting service that publishes a site from a folder or a Git repository, with built-in form handling.
strengths: publishing by dragging a folder in
form handling without extra services
watchOutFor: Free plans have bandwidth and form limits.
Check the terms if the site earns money.

name: Cloudflare Pages
summary: A hosting service from Cloudflare that publishes static and server-rendered sites from Git.
strengths: hosting on a large global network
a custom domain next to Cloudflare's other tools
watchOutFor: Some Next.js features need extra set-up.
Check the free limits before you rely on it.

name: GitHub Pages
summary: Free-to-start hosting for static sites, published straight from a GitHub repository.
strengths: free hosting for static sites from your repository
no separate account if you already use GitHub
watchOutFor: Static files only. There is no server code.
Check its usage limits and terms.

name: Google Analytics
summary: Google's web analytics service that reports who visits a site and what they do there.
strengths: detailed reports on traffic and behaviour
a tool many teams already know
watchOutFor: Many regions require a cookie notice.
The reports can be overwhelming for a small site.

name: Plausible
summary: A simple, privacy-focused web analytics service that shows key numbers on one page.
strengths: one simple page of key numbers
tracking that avoids cookies
watchOutFor: The hosted service may be paid. Self-hosting is possible.
It is less detailed than larger tools.

name: Umami
summary: An open-source, privacy-focused web analytics tool you can host yourself or use as a service.
strengths: open source and self-hostable
simple privacy-friendly tracking
watchOutFor: Self-hosting means you run the server and database.
A hosted version may be paid.

name: Formspree
summary: A service that receives form submissions from a static site and emails them to you.
strengths: a working form on a static site without a server
submissions sent to your email
watchOutFor: Free plans limit the number of submissions.
Add spam protection to the form.

name: Web3Forms
summary: A form back end that sends submissions from a static site to your email with no server of your own.
strengths: a form back end with no server to run
simple set-up with a key in your form
watchOutFor: Check submission limits on free use.
Add spam protection to the form.

name: Google Forms
summary: A free form builder in Google's office suite that collects answers into a spreadsheet.
strengths: free forms with answers collected in a spreadsheet
no code and nothing to host
watchOutFor: It looks like a Google form unless you style the page around it.
You need a Google account.

name: Reactive Resume
summary: A free, open-source resume builder that works in the browser and exports to PDF.
strengths: a free, open-source resume builder
several clean templates
watchOutFor: Check that the exported file opens and copies cleanly.
Keep your own copy of the content.

name: Enhancv
summary: An online resume builder with designed templates and writing suggestions.
strengths: polished, designed templates
prompts that suggest what to write
watchOutFor: Downloads may need a paid plan.
Heavy design can be hard for applicant systems to read.

name: Figma
summary: A browser-based design tool for interface layouts, prototypes and graphics, with real-time sharing.
strengths: shared, real-time design in the browser
a large library of community files
watchOutFor: It takes a while to learn.
Free plans limit files and team features.

name: Penpot
summary: An open-source design and prototyping tool that runs in the browser.
strengths: open-source design that runs in the browser
layouts that map to web code
watchOutFor: The community and plug-in library are smaller than the biggest tools.
Self-hosting means you run the server.

name: Adobe Photoshop
summary: A professional image and photo editor with layers, retouching and design tools.
strengths: deep photo editing and retouching
an industry standard for image work
watchOutFor: It is a subscription product, with a trial rather than a free plan.
It takes time to learn.
